display.purpose: Page title only. One per page.

headline.purpose: Lead phrases that need to sit between display and body, e.g. callout intros.

title.purpose: Roster names. Two points above body because these are the words the room reads through a compressed feed.

body.purpose: Prose — empty-state copy and the completion callout. Default non-numeric text that isn't a name.

caption.purpose: Header meta line, joined-at timestamps, empty-state footnotes. Secondary information the room can ignore.

label.purpose: Small role text on stat tiles, tags, buttons, badges.

numeric.purpose: Live-updating counts and tabular figures. Atkinson Mono with font-feature 'tnum'.

numeric-compact.purpose: Stat-tile counts below 640px, where three full-size numerals would crowd the row.

numeric-row.purpose: The standing position number on each roster row.

numeric-emphasis.purpose: Position number on the up-next row only. Half the up-next signal; the tint is the other half.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions (opacity, color, transform).

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Default duration for hover, focus, and toggle state changes.

motion.name: duration-pulse
motion.purpose: Live-dot halo pulse. Decorative ambient motion, suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview: A small, considered utility that helps the host of a meeting without performing. Every choice on the page is in service of two simultaneous audiences: the host clicking up close, and the whole room watching the screen-share from across a Zoom feed. Nothing is decorative; nothing competes with the conversation in the room. The system is light, warm, and restrained. Paper-coded neutrals carry the canvas. A single sans-serif (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next) handles every text role; tabular numerics use its matching mono. One accent, clay terracotta, exists for moments of attention and is deliberately absent from the state vocabulary itself. State is read through fill density and weight, not color. This system explicitly rejects the gravitational pulls of its category: the dark-navy-and-amber dashboard look the current tracker shipped with, the gamified leaderboard chrome, and the generic SaaS hero-metric template. It also rejects the obvious icebreaker-orange reflex; the warm accent here is clay, not pumpkin.
keyCharacteristics: Light theme, warm paper neutrals, never #fff
Single sans family (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next), single mono (Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono) for numerics
Type is self-hosted, never fetched: the face is part of the build, not a CDN request
One accent (clay), used sparingly and never as a state carrier
Flat by default: no shadows, tonal layering only
Restrained motion: state transitions only, never decorative
Screen-share legibility is the design's first audience

rules.name: The Restrained Accent Rule
rules.body: Clay covers ≤10% of any rendered screen. If you find yourself reaching for a second accent, you're solving the wrong problem. Add weight, label, or tone instead.

rules.name: The Tinted-Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every *neutral* has chroma between 0.005 and 0.022 in the clay hue family. Pure-gray neutrals are forbidden; they break the warm-paper feel and read as cold against the accent. The Up-Next Tint (chroma 0.04) is the one sanctioned exception and is not a neutral: it is a state surface, and adding a second one requires retiring this rule rather than quietly widening it.

rules.name: The No-Hue-Borne-State Rule
rules.body: Introduced vs. waiting is never carried by hue alone. State pairs fill density (paper vs. surface), weight (regular vs. medium), and an explicit icon. A deuteranopic viewer must distinguish the two on first glance.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (plus Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for numerics) is the entire type system. No serif display, no second sans, no icon font carrying glyph weight. Two pairings are retired and must not return: Fraunces + IBM Plex Mono, and the Geist pair that replaced it — the latter was declared but never actually delivered, so the design only existed on machines that happened to have it installed.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerics Rule
rules.body: Every number that updates live (counts on stat tiles, the joined-at timestamp) is rendered in Atkinson Mono with font-feature-settings 'tnum'. Numbers must not reflow their container when they tick.

rules.name: The Self-Hosted Type Rule
rules.body: The face ships from this repo (fonts/, latin subset, ~50KB) and is never fetched from a CDN. Two reasons, and both are binding: a webfont request would break the promise that nothing leaves your machine, and a face that is merely named renders only for whoever already has it. If you change the typeface, you ship the file — declaring a family you do not deliver is the bug this rule exists to prevent.

rules.name: The Screen-Share Floor Rule
rules.body: Body type never goes below 15px. Labels never go below 12px. Anything smaller dies in the 1080p video pipeline. Test by downsampling a screenshot to 1280×720 and reading from 2m away.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If something needs to read as raised, switch its background from paper to surface (tonal layering), don't apply a shadow.

rules.name: The No-Decorative-Glow Rule
rules.body: Backdrop blurs, soft radial-gradient bloom behind hero text, glow-on-hover effects: forbidden. They survive a Figma file; they don't survive a screen-share.

dos: Do use Paper (#faf7f2) for the canvas and default row; Surface (#f3eee5) as the only second tonal layer.
Do carry the introduced-vs-waiting distinction in fill density + weight + icon. State must be legible on a deuteranopic monitor.
Do keep Clay accent under 10% of any rendered screen. Use it for the live dot, focus outlines, and the host identity label only.
Do render every live-updating number in Atkinson Mono with font-feature-settings 'tnum'.
Do test every screen by downsampling a screenshot to 1280×720 and reading it from 2m away.
Do treat reduced-motion as a hard mode switch: live dot stops pulsing, transitions drop to opacity-only, roster updates without animation.
donts: Don't ship a dark theme variant. The page is screen-shared into lit conference rooms.
Don't use #fff or #000. Every neutral is tinted toward the clay hue.
Don't use the green-vs-amber state vocabulary the previous tracker shipped with. Color-blind viewers can't distinguish them.
Don't reach for the generic SaaS dashboard idioms: hero-metric tiles with gradient accents, identical card grids, navy-and-indigo palette.
Don't introduce gamified-leaderboard chrome: avatars, points, badges, ordering by speed.
Don't mimic Zoom or Slack chrome. The page is shared inside Zoom; it should feel like a separate, calmer artifact.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored stripe.
Don't put the 'still to go' people in a warning-colored frame.
Don't animate layout properties. Transitions are opacity, color, and transform only, ease-out-quart 150–200ms.
Don't add an icon font, decorative SVG illustration, or hero image.
